name: Apache IoTDB
tagline: Apache time-series database for industrial IoT with tree and table models and edge-to-cloud sync.
description: Apache IoTDB is a time-series database that came out of Tsinghua University and became an Apache top-level project in 2020. It stores data in its own TsFile columnar format and offers two models: a hierarchical tree of device paths (root.plant.line1.temp) and, since 2.0, a relational table model queried with standard SQL. It is designed to run on edge gateways and synchronise to cloud clusters through its Pipe framework, and integrates with Spark, Flink and Grafana. Timecho, founded by the original authors, sells an enterprise distribution and support.

pricing.notes: Free under Apache-2.0; Timecho sells an enterprise edition and support.

scale.notes: ConfigNodes manage metadata and DataNodes hold partitioned regions replicated via Ratis or IoTConsensus.

strengths: TsFile columnar format with strong compression for sensor data
Lightweight enough for edge gateways, with Pipe-based edge-to-cloud replication
Tree model maps naturally onto plant, line and device hierarchies
Table model in 2.x brings standard SQL and joins
weaknesses: Two data models and two SQL dialects make docs and tooling confusing
JVM footprint and tuning compared with C/Rust-based competitors
Most production references are in China
No managed cloud service from the Apache project itself
useCases: Power plant and wind turbine monitoring
Edge gateways syncing to a central cluster
notIdealFor: Teams wanting a fully managed SaaS
